transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-11
Time: 15:00 - 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Meadowlark Eng Manager), Tom Ellis (Meadowlark CTO), Maya Singh (Meadowlark SRE)
---
Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and lookahead (prefix/KV) caching recommendations for Meadowlark's document summarization service. Ran through a cost sandbox scenario, rough latency budgets, and security controls (KMS/SOC 2). Agreed to run a 1k QPS sim with provided traffic mix and share a cost sandbox spreadsheet.
Topics covered:
- Traffic profile and current costs
- Batching strategies (continuous batching, max batch size, latency SLO tradeoffs)
- Lookahead/prefix KV cache heuristics and hit-rate modeling
- Hybrid routing: hosted vs dedicated, and failover policies
- Security/compliance: KMS keys, audit logs, SOC 2
Action items (listed separately below)
---
Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Okay everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros? I'll do a super-fast agenda — cost sandbox, batching + lookahead cache, then Qs and next steps.
[00:10] Priya: Hi, Priya here. we run the doc-summarization pipeline for legal ingest, so low latency-ish matters, but costs are ballooning.
[00:18] Tom: Tom Ellis, CTO. we're worried about both token spend and concurrency limits, especially during batch ingest windows.
[00:24] Maya: Maya, SRE. I'll be the person running the sim and giving logs.
[00:28] Samir (SE): Samir here, I'll walk through the Optimize console and the KV heuristics. a lot of the talk will be around hit-rates, prefix distribution, and when prefetch/lookahead actually helps.
[00:36] Alex: Great. Priya, can you summarize current traffic — tokens per request, concurrency, percent of requests that have long shared prefixes?
[00:44] Priya: Sure. average request is 1.8k tokens because customers paste long transcripts, but production truncation keeps it ~1.2k for the models we use. concurrency peaks at about 600 concurrent users during EU business hours. approx 22% of requests share a common prefix (like same client meta, same doc header), and a small subset — maybe 3% — are session re-runs where the prefix is identical.
[01:10] Samir: That distribution actually maps well to a hybrid strategy. if you can capture the 3% identical prefixes with a strong KV prefix cache, and the 22% with partial matches using lookahead heuristics, you can reclaim a lot of token cost. rough math: with a 30% cache hit on prefixes your per-token cost drops significantly because KV hits avoid repeated model decode.
[01:30] Tom: When you say "lookahead", do you mean prefetching the KV for likely next tokens or storing the prefix state so that you don't re-run the same prefix?
[01:36] Samir: Both are possible. in Redwood's runtime Optimize module, lookahead primarily means pre-populating the KV cache for probable continuation chunks and storing prefix KV snapshots. for identical prefixes that's instant hit; for partial matches we can do a delta-run. the console shows a hit-rate estimator based on the 90-day prefix histogram you feed in.
[01:58] Priya: We haven't prepared that histogram in detail yet, but we can export 30 days quickly.
[02:04] Alex: Perfect. We'll use that to run the sandbox. quick demo now — Samir?
[02:10] Samir: Switching to my screen. starting with the Optimize tab -> Cost Sandbox. here's our baseline: model: Llama-7B-quant, token price X, avg length 1.2k, concurrency 600, hit-rate 0% -> monthly estimate $35k. now add batching: continuous batching with max batch 32 and latency SLO 200ms. that reduces per-token overhead a bit.
[02:38] Samir: If we enable batching only — assuming sequence lengths and batching efficiency of ~2x tokens-per-gpu-second — we drop to $27k. adding KV prefix cache with a projected 18% hit rate drops to $19kish. note these numbers are illustrative but mirror earlier customers.
[02:55] Maya: quick clarification: does the KV cache live in-memory on the serving node or is it externalized?
[03:02] Samir: Good Q. by default it's node-local in the dedicated pools for fastest lookups; in hosted mode we shard and replicate cache state across nodes with an LRU eviction. there is an option to persist hot snapshots to a backing store (S3/RDS) for warm restarts but that adds small IO latency.
[03:20] Tom: For our compliance needs we'd prefer customer-managed KMS and tight auditing. does cache state get wrapped with encryption keys?
[03:27] Samir: Yes — the Private offering supports envelope encryption with customer KMS, and audit logs include cache priming events. We'll attach the SOC 2/KMS note to the follow-up.
[03:36] Priya: What's the impact on tail latency when you prefetch? I'm worried about spikes where prefetch floods the cluster.
[03:44] Samir: Lookahead prefetch is controlled by a budget policy — you can set concurrent prefetchs per node and a max token budget. in our sandbox we suggested a conservative budget for Meadowlark: prefetch cap of 10 concurrent operations per GPU, and a token cap of 50k tokens/sec overall. that kept 95th percentile latency within SLO during our sim.
[04:08] Priya: That token cap sounds useful — can the Console show live burn rate?
[04:12] Samir: Yep — Console -> Optimize -> Prefetch Insights shows burn rate, estimated costs, and a predicted impact on p50/p95.
[04:20] Alex: Let's go through one specific scenario: heavy ingest window at 800rps for 10 minutes with a 40% prefix overlap. what do we expect?
[04:30] Samir: I ran that scenario in the sandbox earlier: with batching only we get throughput up but cost is still high due to repeated decode on shared prefixes. adding a lightweight prefix cache + delta-run model you get ~38% cost reduction vs baseline and p95 improves by ~60ms on average. if you push prefetch too aggressively you can improve hit-rate further but tail latency can regress unless you increase GPU headroom or set prefetch rate limits.
[04:58] Tom: This delta-run approach — is it model-agnostic? we use a custom fine-tuned Mistral variant.
[05:04] Samir: It's mostly model-agnostic so long as the model uses standard KV caching semantics. we do have model-specific kernel paths that affect performance; the Optimize engine profiles model rollout and suggests quantization only if quality delta is acceptable. we'll run a QC pass on your finetuned variant during the pilot.
[05:22] Priya: You mentioned quantization — does that interplay with cache hit semantics?
[05:26] Samir: Slightly. quantized runtimes can change per-token compute, but KV cache is format-agnostic; you still store key/value pairs. what changes is kernel performance on decode side. Optimize will simulate cost with quantized and non-quantized profiles.
[05:40] Alex: Let's pause — any procurement or legal folks on the call? we should note certification expectations.
[05:45] Priya: No, but procurement will review SOC 2 and the data residency notes.
[05:48] Alex: We'll include that in the follow-up. back to the console demo — Samir?
[05:52] Samir: Showing the Prefetch policy editor. you can tune: lookahead depth (#tokens prefetched), candidate-score threshold, concurrent prefetch per-GPU, and backpressure rules that trigger when GPU util is over 80%. also a fallback route: if prefetch fails we can fallback to a cheaper model or queue for later decoding.
[06:14] Maya: Curious how we instrument quality regressions on delta-run. if the delta changes outputs slightly, how do you monitor?
[06:21] Samir: We integrate with Redwood Optimize's quality monitors — prompt-set based evaluation that runs in canary traffic. we can tie regressions to rollout policies. you'll get alerts if output BLEU-like metrics degrade or if user-facing signals (like edit rate) rise.
[06:36] Priya: Good. What's a realistic timeline for a pilot: sandbox -> bench -> pilot?
[06:41] Alex: Typical is 1 week to share sandbox results after we get the prefix histogram and sample traffic, 1 week to run a 1k QPS sim and a 2-week pilot with small dedicated pool. so about 4–5 weeks for end-to-end if procurement moves quickly.
[06:56] Tom: Cost wise, are there any up-front reserves for the dedicated pool?
[07:00] Alex: For dedicated yes — we propose a reserved baseline for predictability but you can start hosted and then commit to dedicated once the pilot validates. the Optimize recommendations will show the break-even point.
[07:10] Priya: Can you walk through a concrete row from the cost spreadsheet? I'd like to capture the assumptions.
[07:15] Samir: Sure. here's a single-row example: baseline model cost = $0.0025 per 1k tokens (placeholder), avg tokens per request = 1.2k, requests/day = 200k, baseline monthly = tokens * price => $36k. continuous batching reduces cpu overhead by 20% => $28.8k. prefix KV cache hit-rate 18% removes full decode for those requests => $21.8k. enabling lookahead prefetch to push hit-rate to 26% reduces to ~$17.5k but adds modest prefetch cost (~$600) that we net out. those numbers are approximations; we'll replace with your exact pricing/usage in the sandbox.
[07:56] Priya: The numbers help. Is there a built-in ROI calc if we switch to dedicated GPUs with reserved pricing?
[08:02] Samir: Yes — Cost Sandbox has a "dedicated vs hosted" tab. you provide reserved node price and expected utilization and it computes crossover. with the pilot numbers we saw, dedicated breaks even after ~5 months at 65% utilization for similar workloads.
[08:19] Tom: Any risks or gotchas we should be aware of?
[08:21] Samir: A few: incorrectly tuned prefetch can increase token burn if traffic is noisy; eviction policies matter — LRU vs freq-based change hit-rate behaviour; and model divergence on delta-runs if fine-tuning changed the attention kernels. we'll validate those in the sim.
[08:37] Maya: For the simulation we need a runbook. what's the best artifact to attach?
[08:42] Alex: We'll share a short runbook: what logs to collect, a traffic exporter config, and the cost sandbox link.
[08:48] Priya: Can you also include how audit logs are delivered? we need them for SOC 2.
[08:52] Samir: Yes — audit logs are available via S3 delivery or pushed to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). KMS key rotation and key-wrapping details will be in the security note.
[09:02] Tom: I saw "fallback to cheaper model" mentioned. can Redwood automatically fall back when capacity is saturated?
[09:08] Samir: Absolutely — routing policies allow failover to a smaller quantized model or to burst to Dedicated. we can set per-route latency and quality thresholds that drive fallback. that ensures graceful degradation vs hard failures.
[09:22] Priya: Let's talk about metrics we'll use to determine success. besides cost reduction, we care about p95 latency, edit rate, and throughput during ingest windows.
[09:31] Alex: Good set. we'll instrument those. also add cache hit-rate and prefetch burn rate.
[09:36] Samir: I'll add those as default monitors in the sandbox.
[09:40] Priya: Any notable mentions of competitors? we evaluated OtherCloudAI last quarter and they had a similar prefetch feature but their Console didn't show burn metrics.
[09:49] Samir: Right — we've heard that. Redwood's differentiator here is the end-to-end cost sandbox + traceable prefetch metrics and the private deployment options with full KMS control.
[09:59] Tom: Okay next steps recap?
[10:02] Alex: Alex: we'll send the cost sandbox and SOC2/KMS note. Samir: will prep the 1k QPS sim VM and the prefix cache heatmap. Priya: will export 30-day prefix histogram and provide the sample traffic generator. schedule benchmark next Tuesday (2027-03-16) morning UTC.
[10:22] Priya: sounds good. one more question — how much engineering time to integrate SDKs?
[10:26] Samir: Minimal for initial test — a few days to wire traffic exporter and set routing. for deeper integrations like session affinity and persisted snapshots maybe 2–3 sprints.
[10:36] Tom: sounds reasonable.
[10:39] Alex: Great — we'll follow up. thanks everyone.
